replication.target_description: Ahr et al. (2016), p.162 (PDF p.6), response-time negative priming for identical animal probes following mirror versus nonmirror letters. Three separate grade-specific t tests are printed; supplied description does not identify grade. Replication uses f/t and g/j controls and only animal probes, unlike original a/h and animal/building conditions.

reported_success.location: p.163 Discussion, paragraph 1; narrative verdict for negative priming across all three grades, not a uniquely identified grade/outcome

notes: Blind inputs 1828,1829,1830 have identical descriptions, study and page locators and no grade/sample identifiers. No grade assignment based on ID/input order. Located candidates at p.162: first graders t(31)=2.27,p<.05,d=0.20; third graders t(22)=2.43,p<.05,d=0.20; fifth graders t(25)=4.08,p<.001,d=.37. These are distinct tests and cannot be uniquely matched. p.160 explicitly states final grade samples 31,22,25; printed t degrees of freedom are also 31,22,25, a discrepancy retained without correcting or inferring n=df+1. Exclusion at chance prime/probe performance; RT outlier filtering at p.161. Group-specific analytic n cannot be assigned without the missing grade identifier.
